The same reader is applied to a session created WITHOUT a mode, which reports `coding`: an A/B on one reader against two create payloads, in one run, is what makes the chat assertion discriminating (2 passed, 7.0m, both cases). provider-scenario-scripts.scope: streaming success + tool-call/HTTP-failure/SSE-interruption/duplicate/slow scripts. S5 landed the streaming-success script (orchestrator provider) plus /e4/provider-requests dispatch evidence, and the remaining scenarios stay unwritten until a spec needs them. UPDATE 2026-09-19, two families landed with the specs that needed them. (1) HTTP failure: `POST /e4/provider-failures?count=N` arms the next N completion requests to answer a real 5xx inside a real turn (a query parameter, not a body, matching /e4/admission); `e2e/real/session-turn.spec.ts` drives both halves — the armed case asserts the retry surface becomes visible (`[data-slot="session-turn-retry"]`, from the backend's own `SessionRetry.policy` status), that the turn then lands with no second prompt and no reload, and that the provider was asked exactly 3 times; a control asserts exactly 1 with nothing armed. Retryability is not assumed: a status >= 500 is retryable regardless of the provider SDK's own flag (`packages/aigcfroge/src/session/retry.ts:74`), and the turn path sets SDK `maxRetries` to 0 (`prompt.ts:1545`), so the count is the product's own retries. (2) Interrupted stream: the same knob with `mode=sse-cut` writes one delta and then destroys the socket with no finish reason and no `[DONE]`, so no HTTP status exists to classify; an unknown mode is refused with 400 rather than defaulted. MEASURED before asserting — the first run printed `retry=1 error=0` — so a terminated stream is retryable and is not claimed as a failure; the case pins the retry surface, the absence of an error row, exactly 2 completions (the cut plus the attempt that recovered), and that a later turn still reaches the provider (the interruption does not wedge the session). Still unwritten: tool call, duplicate/out-of-order, slow response.
provider-scenario-scripts.unlock: each REMAINING scenario (tool call, duplicate/out-of-order, slow response) is added with the spec that needs it. §12.4's provider failure/recovery is now delivered for both families that have a knob — a classifyable status (5xx) and an unclassifyable termination (cut stream). What remains is the variance family, which needs its own harness knobs (a scripted tool call, duplicated or reordered chunks, a delayed first chunk) before it can have a spec.

e2e-readiness-predicate-flake.scope: e2e/utils/waits.ts expectDevServerReady polls /@vite/client from inside the test and intermittently times out at 120s on this host while the same URL answers in ~25ms from a shell; three occurrences in one session, each passing on rerun. Adjacent, the 180s per-test budget is sometimes too small for the heaviest cases on this host. The mechanism is recorded with its correction in docs/technical-debt.md §8 (`冷态 dev server 的首轮编译会顶穿就绪探测预算`): the cold first round compiles on the server's single event loop, so even static paths queue, and the case that pays for it is the FIRST of the round — re-measured during S7, where warming `/` alone took 293s while every later route took 7-10s, and a run that warmed only `/` still stalled on its second navigation.
e2e-readiness-predicate-flake.unlock: keep the readiness signal honest and stop paying the cold round per suite: either give the first case of a round its own budget (the ledger's second option), or land the ledger's first option — warm the target routes (including a session-detail route, which is where the mode content panels compile) to first paint before the round. S7 warmed with a scratch script outside the harness; the fix belongs in the harness's global setup. The ledger explicitly rules out enlarging APP_READY_TIMEOUT globally, because that also slows catching a server that is genuinely down.

STATUS 2026-09-19, two halves decided differently. (b) SCROLL: CLOSED with a measured green. The mode mock now serves 40 turns (`mode-slot-fallback-a11y.spec.ts:472-505`), the new case `opening and closing the floating panel leaves the timeline's scroll offset alone` (`:509-568`) asserts the fixture really overflows, moves the offset with a real wheel gesture, opens and closes the overlay, and then asserts BOTH that the same element is still mounted (`data-scroll-probe`) and that the offset is unchanged. Run: ext4 worktree `/home/keer/s8w` at 5473f53a8, private port, workers=1, no retries, `bun run test:e2e -- e2e/regression/mode-slot-fallback-a11y.spec.ts --project=chromium` -> 15 passed (38.6s), the new case alone -> 1 passed (18.9s). DISCRIMINATING, verified by mutation rather than asserted: forcing `narrowContentPanelOpen()` false in `pages/session.tsx:309-314` turns the new case RED on `the floating panel must mark the session body inert, not remove it` (1 failed); the mutation was reverted and the file confirmed identical to HEAD (`git diff --exit-code`). The mount-preservation half rests on `pages/session.tsx:305-308` plus `:2035` (the column is set `inert`/`aria-hidden`, never `Show`-removed) — that link is read, not mutation-measured, and is reported as such. (a) BACK: still open and now explicitly BLOCKED on a ruling, not on work. The main plan already settles the handling in §22 (`docs/plan/global-shell-product-closure-2026-09-13.md:481`): the protocol text cannot decide whether `back` means browser-back or an in-panel affordance, the two readings have different costs and risks (the former manipulates history and interacts with the fail-closed router and the Dirty Guard), so nothing is guessed and nothing is implemented until one explicit decision. Consistent with that, the panel's open state is deliberately not in the URL, so browser-back would currently leave the Session rather than close the overlay. CORRECTION 2026-09-19: an earlier manifest edit in the same session registered `real-200-percent-zoom` as an open S7 gap, on the strength of the manual's §2 list. That was WRONG and has been removed: the requirement is delivered and was re-verified by running it, not by reading the old report. `packages/app/e2e/zoom/` (committed: `narrow-real-zoom.spec.ts`, `zoom-profile.ts`, `fixtures.ts`, its own config) seeds `Default/Preferences` with `per_host_zoom_levels.x."127.0.0.1".zoom_level` and launches the real `chromium` channel with `viewport: null`, and the spec asserts the four measurements that make it real zoom (innerWidth 720 vs window 1440, DPR 2, mq768 false, and a 1200px probe going from non-overflowing to overflowing) BEFORE it touches the app. Run: `PLAYWRIGHT_PORT=3082 bun run test:e2e:zoom -- --reporter=line` -> 2 passed (10.9s), the second being `a seeded profile zooms, reflows, and must keep the mode panels reachable` and the first the control that proves the seed - not the window size - is what zooms. The manual's §2 snapshot is stale on this item; the recipe stays documented in `docs/review/global-shell-remaining-closure.md` §4.3.
mode-panel-back-and-scroll.unlock: (b) nothing further is owed. (a) one Owner decision is required, and it is the ONLY thing blocking this entry: does `back` dismiss the narrow overlay (implying the overlay must participate in history, with the Dirty Guard interaction that entails), or does back keep navigating and the overlay stays out of history (in which case the §10 line is satisfied by saying so in the docs and asserting the negative)? Do not implement either reading before that ruling; do not re-open the scroll half.

hidden-panel-request-and-remount.scope: plan §10 listed this under S7 alongside the narrow-panel work, but its subject is render ownership, not narrow layout: a hidden/closed panel must not re-issue requests and must not remount the business owner. This repo keeps hidden surfaces MOUNTED on purpose (render-all + `display:none`, with `ModeSlotActiveProvider` gating side effects), while the secondary sidebar's `Show` really does unmount - two different lifecycles that must not be conflated. STATUS 2026-09-19: COVERED, and the doc half was already done. (1) The plan carries the Owner-agreed scope correction at `docs/plan/global-shell-product-closure-2026-09-13.md:434`, so the line is no longer inherited as narrow-panel work. (2) Node identity for the mode surfaces is now asserted, which the pre-existing check could not do: `mode-surface-wiring.spec.ts:112` used `toHaveCount(1)`, and a count of 1 is satisfied by a FRESH node just as well as by a surviving one. The new case `a mode round trip keeps the same slot nodes and re-issues none of the hidden mode's reads` (`:125-185`) stamps all ten slot nodes (`data-node-probe`, and it asserts the stamp count is 10 first, so an unmounted slot fails at that step), performs the switch the way a user does it - the rail button, i.e. client-side navigation, not `page.goto` - and then requires the SAME node to come back, hidden and visible. (3) Its request half is scoped to chat's own asset lists (`/prompt-asset`, `/skill-asset`, `/mcp-asset`, `/command-asset`, `/plugin-asset`; `/workflow-asset` is excluded because Work reads it too), because the newly shown mode legitimately loads its own data - a blanket 'no requests at all' bound would fail for the right reason and pass for the wrong ones. (4) The second lifecycle is already pinned separately: `mode-slot-fallback-a11y.spec.ts:244-254` asserts the secondary sidebar panel is NOT mounted while closed (count 0), then mounted with `role="complementary"` and `aria-controls` when opened - so the two lifecycles are tested apart rather than folded into one claim. EVIDENCE: ext4 worktree `/home/keer/s8w` at 5473f53a8, private port, workers=1, no retries - the new case alone: 1 passed (14.7s); the whole file: 14 passed (51.3s). NOT claimed: the identity assertion is remount-sensitive by construction (an attribute written to the live node cannot survive a rebuild), but no mutation probe was run for this one, unlike the S7 scroll case; and `chat-asset-categories.spec.ts:154` separately records that a FULL page reload round trip does re-read the lists, which is pre-existing keying behaviour and a different path from this in-app switch.
hidden-panel-request-and-remount.unlock: Nothing further is owed for the mode-surface half: node identity and scoped request counts are asserted, and the plan note exists. If the Owner wants the same mutation-level proof the S7 scroll case got, the cheap probe is to wrap a slot in `Show when={mode.currentMode === slot}` in `mode-workspace.tsx` and confirm this case goes red on the lost stamp - optional, not a gap in the contract. The secondary sidebar's close/reopen lifecycle stays a distinct, already-covered case; do not merge the two into one assertion.

path-identity.scope: plan §11.2 requires a provable path identity, and S8 reconnaissance found there is none anywhere: zero inode/device/sameFile hits across core, schema and aigcfroge; `Project.resolve` (packages/core/src/project.ts:110-122) identifies a project by git remote or root-commit hash, not by path, and every non-git directory collapses to the literal id `global` (packages/core/src/project.ts:112 with packages/core/src/session.ts:448-464); `ProjectDirectoryTable` keys on (project_id, directory) with `directory` realpath'd (packages/core/src/project/directories.ts:65-82), and realpath cannot unify a bind-mount or same-inode alias — the exact `/media/keer/办公/aigcfroge` vs `/media/win_data/aigcfroge` case the review reported; `LocationServiceMap` keys on the raw `Location.Ref` struct (packages/core/src/location-layer.ts:101), so two spellings of one physical directory get two Location-scoped service graphs, and `sameLocation` in packages/core/src/permission/approval-presence.ts:98-100 is raw `===` on the directory string.
path-identity.unlock: its own ADR and backend contract (plan §22-2, approved in principle 2026-09-17; plan §4.3 requires the ADR to land before any migration or endpoint): a resolver that can PROVE identity locally and returns a typed unknown/degraded when it cannot, rather than merging by string equality or by inode alone. Any durable part needs the clean/existing fixture, compatibility decode and forward-only rollback that §4.3 demands. The app must stay out of it: the S8 registry work normalizes spelling only (pathKey) and claims nothing about physical identity.

home-offline-state.scope: DELIVERED with reported evidence, not re-verified by me. Measured first (throwaway spec, before the change): with the focused server unreachable Home rendered its ordinary empty state, count 0, "No sessions found" — and the only failure signal (a per-directory toast) had already expired, so the page could not distinguish unreachable from empty. Treatment: `home-overview.tsx` derives `offlineServer` from the existing `useServerHealth` (undefined means not-yet-checked, so Home never claims offline without evidence), the empty state is guarded by `!offlineServer()`, and an offline notice reusing the app-level unreachable/retrying wording replaces it with 'Manage servers' as the way forward (the existing server dialog). One new i18n key in en/zh/zht. Spec: e2e/regression/home-server-unreachable.spec.ts, 3 tests (unreachable notice and no false empty state; manage-servers opens; healthy-server control). Provenance: the green tally (3 passed, 4.1m) comes from the delegated workstream, which had to run on a private port because port 3000's server was saturated; I did not reproduce it, so it is reported as claim, not as my own verified result. UPDATE 2026-09-18: the tally this entry recorded as someone else's claim is now reproduced first-hand. ext4 worktree at fd7585f38, private port, workers=1, no retries, `bun run test:e2e -- e2e/regression/home-server-unreachable.spec.ts --project=chromium` -> 3 passed (9.9s): `says the server is unreachable instead of claiming the account is empty`, `offers the shell's server-management dialog as the way forward`, `a healthy server still shows the ordinary empty page`. So the code and the spec now both have the green run this entry was missing; the two deliberate omissions below are what is still open. UPDATE 2026-09-19: omission (1) is closed. A fourth case, `keeps cached sessions visible under the offline notice` (`:131`), asserts the additive half the one-shot cases cannot reach — they abort the endpoints before the first load ever succeeds. It loads ONE session from a healthy mock, flips a mutable `offline` switch so the health and session routes start aborting, waits for the health poll (server-health.ts `pollMs` 10s; the 15s budget at `:140` covers one interval), and then asserts the notice is VISIBLE *and* the session row is still visible under it (`:141`). The switch is a box the route handlers consult per request, so all four cases now share the single `openHome` setup. DISCRIMINATING, by mutation rather than by assertion: forcing the group block to `Show when={!offlineServer() && (pinned().pinned || groups().length > 0)}` (`home-overview.tsx:316`) makes that case RED at `:141` with `:140` already green — i.e. the notice appears and the list is what disappears; the mutation was reverted and the file confirmed identical to HEAD. Runs, first-hand, ext4 worktree `/home/keer/s8w` at `87b9d0af2` + this patch, private port 3083, workers=1, no retries: 4 passed (22.0s) before and after the setup refactor.
home-offline-state.unlock: The evidence half is closed, both halves of it: the one-shot offline cases (3 passed, above) and the offline-with-cached-sessions case added 2026-09-19, asserted and mutation-discriminated. Still open and needing a product decision, unchanged: does the offline state owe a retry affordance of its own? Today it says 'Retrying automatically...' and offers 'Manage servers', which is the shared app-level wording rather than a control. That is a product question, not a blocker for the statement this entry was created to make.

project-large-list.scope: MEASURED 2026-09-17, verdict: nothing misbehaves. e2e/regression/project-list-scale.spec.ts seeds the registry directly and reports raw numbers, asserting only contract-shaped things (the app renders exactly N rows, stays interactive, throws no page errors). home-no-project-recovery.scope: MECHANISM PINNED AND FIXED, 2026-09-18: from live instrumented runs on an ext4 checkout, then signed off with an A/B in one environment. CHAIN, each link measured rather than read. (1) The legacy directory picker's search resource threw `TypeError: results.map is not a function`. `directory-picker-domain.ts` read `result.data ?? []` and then called `.map`/`.filter` on it while the SDK declares those bodies as `string[]`/`FileNode[]`, so a body that is not an array threw; the pre-existing `.catch(() => [])` could not help because a 404/JSON error body RESOLVES rather than rejects (in the E2E the mock does not serve `GET /find/file`, so the picker's first, empty-query request is exactly that case). (2) That error is delivered to the app-level `ErrorBoundary` (`app.tsx:521-536` - the only one ABOVE the router; `mode-workspace.tsx:170` and `:193` add two slot-level boundaries INSIDE route content, which is a different position and a different blast radius), which sits ABOVE the router - it wraps `props.children`, i.e. `AppInterface`, which owns `<Dynamic component={props.router ?? Router}>` - and sets its `errored` signal. (3) The navigation that follows runs `@solidjs/router`'s `transition()`, which calls `resetErrorBoundaries()`; clearing `errored` is a real value change, so the boundary's `createMemo` re-runs and re-evaluates `props.children`, RE-CREATING `AppInterface` -> `<Dynamic>` -> a brand-new router context. Measured order: `BOUNDERR b1 results.map is not a function`, then inside the transition `errored = undefined tRunning=true`, then `BOUNDKIDS b1 errored=undefined -> evaluate props.children`, then `router component invoked {seq:2, browserUrl:"/"}`. (4) `createRouter` seeds its source signal from `window.location`, which is still the OLD path because `navigateEnd`'s pushState has not run yet, and the old closure's `.finally` then performs `navigateEnd` -> `setSource` -> `pushState` through the now-dead signal. Net result: project registry, draft tab and browser URL all commit; Home stays mounted; the draft surface never mounts and the lazy `new-session` module is never requested. That is exactly why a reload works and why a SECOND navigation works: by then `errored` is already `undefined`, so the reset notifies nothing and the router survives. FIX (one file, one behaviour): `directory-picker-domain.ts` no longer trusts the declared body type - `isPickerNode` (an `Object.entries` shape walk, no assertions, no `any`), `Array.isArray`, and `typeof path === "string"` - so an unexpected body degrades to 'no rows', exactly like a failed request already did. EVIDENCE, one environment, one variable: ext4 worktree, private port, `bun run test:e2e -- e2e/regression/home-no-project-recovery.spec.ts --project=chromium`, workers=1, no retries, no sleep. Without the guard: 1 failed (9.2s) with the spec's pinned-defect assertion. With the guard: 1 passed (15.7s). Instrumented corroboration: the broken run shows `router component invoked {seq:2}` immediately after the boundary reset; the fixed run shows exactly one router invocation, no `BOUNDERR`, `DraftRoute entered`, and `router state {url:"/new-session?draftId=...", isRouting:false}`. RETRACTIONS of this record's own earlier text: (a) commit 82214ec7d's conclusion 'no Solid transition is ever created' is WRONG. That reading came from instrumenting `solid-js/dist/dev.js` and `dist/solid.js`, which this app does not load - it loads vite's pre-bundled `node_modules/.vite/deps/chunk-*.js`, the same wrong-file trap that had hidden the router's own `dist/index.js`; instrumenting the file that IS loaded shows `Transition.running === true` on the writes made inside the transition body and one `completeUpdates {hasTransition:true, promises:0, queue:0, sources:3}`. (b) 'the location signal reverts to /' was a mis-reading: the write and its read-back are both correct, they simply belong to two different router contexts. (c) The picker's `fallbackPath` resource (`state:"ready", loading:false, missingBase:false`), `DirtyDraftGuard`, the throw/hold/`Transition.promises` lines, and `DraftRoute`'s ready gate plus `Navigate` fallback stay refuted and are not part of this chain.

router-recreated-by-error-boundary-reset.scope: FOUND WHILE FIXING `home-no-project-recovery`, deliberately NOT fixed there because it needs a design decision, not a guard. The app-level `ErrorBoundary` (`app.tsx:521-536`) sits above the router - the only one that does; `mode-workspace.tsx:170` and `:193` are slot-level boundaries inside route content, and `@solidjs/router` calls `resetErrorBoundaries()` inside `transition()` on every navigation. Clearing that boundary's `errored` is a real change, so its `createMemo` re-runs, re-evaluates `props.children`, and re-creates `AppInterface` -> `<Dynamic component={Router}>` - the whole router - as a brand-new context seeded from `window.location` before `navigateEnd` has committed the URL. Consequence: after ANY error that reached that boundary, the NEXT in-app navigation is swallowed - the URL and the persisted state move, the route never renders, and no error is raised. Measured on an ext4 run: `BOUNDERR b1 <error>` -> `errored = undefined tRunning=true` (the router's own reset) -> `router component invoked {seq:2, browserUrl:"/"}` -> `pushState` on the dead context -> silence. A second navigation then works, because `errored` is already `undefined` and the reset notifies nothing; a run with no error at all shows exactly one router invocation, which is why ordinary navigation is unaffected. This is the same root cause the recovery defect escalated through; it is simply reachable from every error, not only from the picker's.
router-recreated-by-error-boundary-reset.unlock: Decide where the boundary belongs, then land it as one change: either move the app-level boundary BELOW the router (so a reset re-renders route content, which is what the router intends) or mount the shell outside the resettable boundary. The trade-off that must be settled explicitly is that the boundary currently also catches errors thrown while `AppInterface` and the providers above the router are constructed - that coverage must not be dropped silently. Verification owed: a spec that (1) provokes one error which reaches that boundary, (2) navigates in-app, (3) asserts the route renders - plus the existing control that an error-free navigation re-creates nothing.
